subject: Initial payload handshake & TTFT acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial payload handshake & TTFT acceptance criteria

Hi Alan / Jenna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested acceptance criteria so we have a clear handoff for the pilot: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: integrate streaming responses for assistant UI with predictable Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and graceful fallback for older clients.
- Preferred streaming path discussed: SSE for simplicity, WebSocket for multiplexing later.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- TTFT target: median <= 180ms; 95th percentile <= 450ms when tested under production-like latency (US-east region).
- Throughput / concurrency: pilot target 20 concurrent streams per instance; sustained 40 requests/sec peak across the cluster.
- Chunk cadence: goal of emitting the first meaningful chunk within TTFT budget, then subsequent chunks at ~150–300ms cadence when possible (small chunks for ultra-low-latency UI).
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to short-polling (2000ms) if SSE disconnects; client reconnect + resume semantics documented.
- Monitoring: per-stream TTFT, chunk-rate histogram, and error-rate dashboards must be available during the soak.

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik to propose the exact chunk framing and reconnection semantics we’ll run in the pilot (technical doc attached).
- Ben to coordinate scheduling for a 48-hour soak once we have the test harness and config.
- Streamline to confirm concurrency expectations and provide a small traffic sample (typical utterance length).

Attachment: SLO-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf) — initial SLO grid and test plan.

If these criteria look right I’ll ask Ben to start the trial agreement and we can lock dates.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

On Mon, Aug 16, 2027 at 9:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick recap and suggested acceptance criteria so we have a clear handoff for the pilot:
> 
> - TTFT target: median <= 180ms; 95th <= 450ms
> - Chunk cadence: ~150–300ms after first chunk

Thanks for the clear summary — a few technical notes from my side before we lock the acceptance test specifics: 

1) SSE vs WebSocket
- SSE: simplest for single-stream-per-connection UIs, built-in reconnection behavior in many clients, lower operational complexity.
- WebSocket: preferred if Streamline expects client multiplexing (multiple chat tabs / multi-user sockets) or binary framing.

2) Chunk framing and payload sizing
- Recommendation: first chunk should carry the first 8–12 tokens / model confidence header so UI can render quickly (saves round-trips).
- Subsequent chunks: aim for 120–200 token windows or time-based flushes at ~150–250ms, whichever comes first. This balances CPU overhead and network overhead.

3) Backpressure and concurrency
- Server should accept a soft concurrency limit per connection (e.g., 1 active stream per WS connection) and global pool-level concurrency (we suggested 20 concurrent streams for pilot).
- If concurrency limit is hit, server will return a 429 with Retry-After; client should queue locally with exponential backoff.

4) Acceptance test specifics (technical)
- Run a 2-hour ramp to 20 concurrent streams, hold for 2 hours at steady-state; measure TTFT (median + 95p) and chunk cadence histograms.
- Network conditions: run tests with baseline latency (10–20ms) and with an added 100ms RTT to simulate cross-region users.
- Success = meet TTFT targets and <1% dropped streams during soak.

I’ll drop a short doc into the Drive link with exact curl/websocket test scripts and the instrumentation keys.

—Karthik

karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear plan. We reviewed internally and can confirm the following from Streamline’s side: 

- Streaming approach: we prefer SSE initially (clients are browser-only for pilot); we can consider WS in phase 2.
- Concurrency: our web tier can sustain ~25 concurrent user streams per app server (we’ll provision two app servers for the pilot).
- Typical payloads: median utterance ~320 tokens, peak bursts up to ~900 tokens for long summaries.
- Network: attached is our network-topology-diagram.png showing routing and NAT timeouts.

Acceptance tests: we agree to the 2-hour ramp + 2-hour soak. One clarification: for the TTFT target, can Redwood measure TTFT both at the edge (Redwood ingress) and end-to-end (client-observed first byte)? We want both numbers in the report.

Also: we can run an internal client-side harness to replay real traffic; we’ll share a 1-hour sample trace (anonymized).

Small ask on reconnection: our current browsers close idle SSE connections after 6 minutes; can the pilot include a keepalive/heartbeat event every 30s to keep paths alive?

If that all sounds right Ben — please send over the trial agreement and proposed start dates.

Cheers,
Alan Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Streamline AI
alan@streamline.ai

Attachment: network-topology-diagram.png (png)

Alan / Jenna —

Perfect — thanks for confirming the concurrency and the sample trace. A few concrete actions and dates so we move quickly: 

Action items:
- Ben: please create the two-week pilot agreement and send DocuSign link to Streamline by EOD Wednesday (attachment: trial-agreement-docusign.pdf).
- Karthik: prepare the test harness and the Drive folder with scripts + instrumentation keys by Thursday; include both edge and client-measured TTFT metrics.
- Streamline: share the 1-hour anonymized traffic sample and confirm the pilot start window (we’re proposing Aug 23–Aug 25 for the soak).

Pilot defaults we’re locking in:
- Streaming: SSE with 30s heartbeat events to avoid intermediate NAT/idle drops.
- TTFT measurement: report both Redwood ingress TTFT and client-observed time-to-first-byte.
- Chunk cadence: first chunk targeted within 180ms, then subsequent chunks flushed at 150–250ms or 150–200 tokens.

Ben will follow up with pricing and a short commercial trial addendum. If we hit the TTFT/soak targets we’ll discuss expanding to WebSocket multiplexing in phase 2.

Thanks all — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
